jurisdiction.name: Slovenia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Slovenia implements the EU AI Act through a 2025 law (ZIUDHPUI) that sets up five market surveillance authorities, an AI regulatory sandbox run by the communications regulator AKOS, a mandatory register of AI systems in the public sector (published as open data in 2026) and a national council for AI ethics. Policy follows the National AI Strategy to 2030, adopted in March 2026 and replacing the 2021 national AI programme. The Ministry of Digital Transformation has issued guidelines on AI in public administration and the Information Commissioner has issued recommendations for public servants using AI at work.
lead_institutions: Agency for Communication Networks and Services (AKOS)
Government of the Republic of Slovenia
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. One guidance document could only be located because its portal does not serve text without a login, and the strategy's action plans are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Nacionalna strategija za umetno inteligenco do leta 2030 (NsUI 2030)
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the Republic of Slovenia (prepared by the Ministry of Digital Transformation)
instruments.publisher_name: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Government on 5 March 2026 (stated on the gov.si project page; period 5.3.2026-31.12.2029, status 'V teku'). It upgrades the NpUI 2025. An official English version (NsUI2030_ang) and an annex on vulnerable groups are published on the same page. The page lists the Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration as responsible institution, while the strategy names the Ministry of Digital Transformation as national manager. A draft was put to public consultation in November 2025 under the name NpUI 2030.
instruments.summary: Slovenia's national AI strategy, adopted by the Government on 5 March 2026, succeeding the National Programme for AI to 2025. It sets ten guiding principles and five strategic goals (sovereign and trustworthy AI capacity; uptake in the economy, science, public sector and civil society; knowledge and ecosystem; security, resilience and defence; international standing) built on six horizontal building blocks, including ethics and regulation. Governance rests with the Ministry of Digital Transformation as national strategy manager, an inter-ministerial coordination group, a Government Council for AI and an AI Observatory, with measures to follow in action plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; defines the national AI governance structure and responds to generative AI and the EU AI Act.

Contact organisation is the Ministry of Digital Transformation; OPSI lists the Ministry of the Interior and Public Administration as publisher. The required fields are set by ZIUDHPUI art. 21.
instruments.summary: Official national register (single information point) through which public-sector bodies report the AI systems and AI-based IT solutions they use, established under art. 21 of ZIUDHPUI. Entries cover the body using the system, intended use and effects, basic principles of the algorithms, references to data protection and fundamental-rights impact assessments, and available legal remedies. Reporting is done through an e-service on the SPOT portal and the collection is published as open data (CC BY 4.0).

instruments.summary: Slovenia's first national AI programme, confirmed by the Government on 27 May 2021 (and earlier by the ministry on 18 December 2020), prepared under the lead of the Ministry of Public Administration. It set strategic objectives covering the AI ecosystem, education, research, reference solutions, infrastructure, security, public trust, the legal and ethical framework and international cooperation to 2025. It was succeeded by the National AI Strategy to 2030 adopted on 5 March 2026.

instruments.official_title: Zakon o izvajanju uredbe (EU) o določitvi harmoniziranih pravil o umetni inteligenci (ZIUDHPUI)
instruments.english_title: Act Implementing the Regulation (EU) Laying Down Harmonised Rules on Artificial Intelligence (ZIUDHPUI)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia
instruments.current_status: In force since 21 November 2025 (art. 45: fifteenth day after publication on 6 November 2025). Transitional deadlines: single information point within two months, first sandbox by 2 August 2026 (art. 40; AKOS's June 2026 call notes the EU digital omnibus extends this to 2 August 2027), first call for ethics council members within 60 days.
instruments.summary: National implementing act for the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), adopted by the National Assembly on 23 October 2025 and published in Uradni list RS No. 85/2025. It designates notifying authorities and five market surveillance authorities (AKOS as single point of contact, the Information Commissioner for prohibited practices and several Annex III areas, the Bank of Slovenia, the Insurance Supervision Agency and the Market Inspectorate), makes AKOS responsible for AI regulatory sandboxes, sets misdemeanour fines, and requires public-sector bodies to publish data on the AI systems they use at a single information point (art. 21). It also establishes a five-member National Council for Ethics in AI appointed by the Government (art. 23).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Core national AI law: designates AI Act authorities, mandates the public-sector AI register and creates the national AI ethics council.

instruments.current_status: In force from 26 January 2023 (art. 127: thirtieth day after publication on 27 December 2022). Later amendments (e.g. 2025) not reviewed here; consolidated text on PISRS.
instruments.summary: Slovenia's general data protection act implementing and supplementing the GDPR, adopted on 15 December 2022 and published in Uradni list RS No. 163/2022, replacing ZVOP-1 (2004). It governs processing of personal data wholly or partly by automated means, including national rules on biometrics, video surveillance and public-sector processing, and the Information Commissioner's supervision. It is the national data protection framework that applies to AI training and use involving personal data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National data protection law framing personal-data processing by AI systems; supervised by the Information Commissioner.

instruments.official_title: Smernice za razvoj, uvedbo in uporabo umetne inteligence v javni upravi
instruments.english_title: Guidelines for the Development, Introduction and Use of Artificial Intelligence in Public Administration
instruments.current_status: Adoption announced by the Ministry on gov.si on 17 March 2026; the document (release 2.0) is published on the ministry's NIO portal. Exact adoption date not stated in the announcement.
instruments.summary: Guidelines adopted by the Ministry of Digital Transformation for public administration bodies acting as deployers and providers of AI systems, giving practical, legal and ethical starting points for AI in internal processes and in services to citizens and businesses. Annex 1 gives recommendations to public employees on using publicly available generative AI tools; Annex 2 sets an exit strategy for cloud services and security requirements and recommendations for processing protected data in AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Central government guidance on public-sector AI use, including generative AI and AI security.

instruments.official_title: Varna in odgovorna uporaba umetne inteligence pri delu – Priporočila za javne uslužbence
instruments.english_title: Safe and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence at Work – Recommendations for Public Servants
instruments.issuing_authority: Information Commissioner of the Republic of Slovenia
instruments.publisher_name: Information Commissioner of the Republic of Slovenia
instruments.current_status: Published on the Information Commissioner's AI 'Guidelines and recommendations' page; the PDF file name is dated 10 February 2026 (no date in the text). The Commissioner also publishes individual opinions on AI (e.g. 14 January, 20 January and 6 February 2026).
instruments.summary: Two-page recommendations from the Information Commissioner to public servants using AI tools at work. They advise checking the body's internal rules before using AI tools, not entering personal, confidential or other protected data unless the processing is lawful and specifically provided for, minimising data, and recognising that deleting obvious identifiers is not anonymisation. They also require users to verify outputs for errors (hallucinations) and bias and to keep final decisions and responsibility with humans.

instruments.english_title: Public Call for Proposals on the Subject Area of the Artificial Intelligence Regulatory Sandbox
instruments.issuing_authority: Agency for Communication Networks and Services of the Republic of Slovenia (AKOS)
instruments.publisher_name: Agency for Communication Networks and Services of the Republic of Slovenia
instruments.current_status: Call No. 38292-2/2026/2 dated 12 June 2026. It notes the statutory deadline for the first sandbox (2 August 2026) is extended to 2 August 2027 by the EU digital omnibus on AI. Outcome (selected subject area) not yet published as of 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Public call by AKOS, issued under art. 17 of ZIUDHPUI, inviting companies, research bodies, public bodies and individuals to propose the subject area (from AI Act Annex I section A or Annex III) of Slovenia's first AI regulatory sandbox. It describes a two-phase process: selecting the sandbox subject area through this call, then a separate call to select AI systems for testing. Expressions of interest do not guarantee participation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First step in establishing the national AI Act regulatory sandbox.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. NIO portal builds pages in the browser and its API needs a login (MDP guidelines located only, date from the 17 March 2026 announcement). gov.si AI ethics council page timed out. Bank of Slovenia, Insurance Supervision Agency, Market Inspectorate, SIST and URSIV/SI-CERT only at discovery level. Ministry responsibility unclear (MDP vs MNZJU, possible 2026 reorganisation). Convention 108: Uradni list RS 11/1994 (MP 3/1994), recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: Uradni list RS: ZIUDHPUI (AI Act implementing law, 85/2025) and ZVOP-2 (163/2022) read in full/key parts; Convention 108 ratification act (MP 3/1994) located. No standalone AI bill or deepfake-specific offence found in the time box.; Government: Government/MDP: NsUI 2030 (2026), NpUI 2025 (2021), MDP public-administration AI guidelines (2026, NIO portal), OPSI public-sector AI register.; Ministries: Searched education/science (gov.si 2024 news on generative-AI research guidelines refers to EU ERA-forum guidelines, not a national document), other ministries: no ministry-specific AI documents found in the time box.; Regulators: Information Commissioner (AI section: recommendations for public servants; individual AI opinions), AKOS (sandbox call). Bank of Slovenia, Insurance Supervision Agency, Market Inspectorate, SI-CERT/URSIV, SIST: no AI-specific documents found (not deeply searched).. Not reached: Bank of Slovenia / Insurance Supervision Agency AI supervisory documents (only discovery level); National standards body SIST adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 (one search, no SIST page found); Government Office for Information Security (URSIV) AI security guidance (not checked); National Council for Ethics in AI page (timed out). Could not verify: Full text of MDP 'Smernice za razvoj, uvedbo in uporabo UI v javni upravi' (NIO portal is client-side and its API needs a session; curl and WebFetch both returned no content); National Council for Ethics in AI working-body page (curl timed out). procurement, standards, index-readiness, sectoral, international: no material found.
